component.create.params: name?, parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); parent_path?: exact parent placement; activate?: bool (default true); grounded?: bool (default: true for the design's first part, false otherwise)

component.insert_design.params: path: a .sc design → a new component linked to it, holding its solid bodies as placed in that design and a copy of its design properties; configuration?: a row name or id (null or omitted: the saved source state); name? (default: the design's name); parent?: component id or name (default: the active one); translate?: [x,y,z] in mm from the destination parent's origin (default [0,0,0], also with reuse); reuse?: bool (default false): insert a free occurrence, reusing an existing link to the same file and configuration when available

component.metadata.set.params: component: id or name (not the root: use document.metadata.set); part_number?, description?, revision?: text (empty or null removes); bom_type?: normal|phantom|reference|purchased|inseparable (empty or null: normal); values?: {key: value} (SolidCraft's keys, as document.metadata's properties lists them, bom_type, or a reverse-DNS key holding an object); properties?: {name: text, …} (free properties; empty or null removes). All or nothing, one undo step → component, metadata, properties, changed: [keys]

config.activate.params: row: a row's name, or its id from config.table — sets its parameter values and suppressions

config.column.params: param? | feature? | material? | appearance? (target name); delete?: bool

config.row.params: name (a row's name, or its id from config.table); from? (row to copy, by name or id; default current values); values?: {column key: expression, suppression, material name, appearance name or Look object}; rename?; delete?: bool

document.metadata.set.params: key and value, or values: {key: value, …} (all or nothing, one undo step). SolidCraft's keys, the ones document.metadata's properties lists, take text ("" or null removes); another tool's data goes under its reverse-DNS key such as com.example.tool (an object; null removes) → metadata, changed: [keys]

document.units.params: units: mm|cm|m|in|ft (display and unit-less parameters; values keep their meaning)

joint.create.params: type: rigid|revolute|slider|cylindrical|pin_slot|planar|ball, or a relation: parallel|perpendicular|angle|point_on_plane|point_on_line|line_on_plane (ties only some directions or points, made where the parts are; several between two parts add up); a, b: joint origins ({occurrence, face|circle|edge|point: [x,y,z] in world, or face|circle: "<face name>", plane: "XY"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>", axis: "Z"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>"; z? for a point, end?, x? as joint.origin} | origin name); values?: [angles in deg or expressions, distances]; limits?: [[min, max] | null…]; flip?: bool (default false: the origins are mated, b's z against a's as two faces meet - two plane or axis datums mate aligned, each part keeping its side of the datum, and flip mates them; true: b's z along a's, so two origins given at one point with the same z and x stay as they are; a point origin without x takes its x from z, so give x on both, or use joint.as_built, to keep a turned part where it is); offset_x?, offset_y?: lateral mm in a's frame (expressions evaluated once); offset?: mm or an expression; angle?: deg or an expression (an angle relation's tilt from mated; for other joints the default is

joint.limits.params: joint; index?: value index (default 0); min?, max? (omit both to clear)

joint.motion_link.params: a, b: joints; ratio (b = ratio · a + offset): b's units per a's (mm per deg for an angle driving a distance); offset?: in b's units (deg for an angle, mm for a distance, or an expression); ia?, ib?: value indices (default 0); link?: index (put this link in place of that motion link, as the gear and cam commands do) → link: the link's index, as joint.list numbers them

joint.origin.params: name?, occurrence?: id|name (default: from the pick, or the named face's component), path?: [occurrence ids from the root] (the placement picked on, ending at the occurrence: a part in a sub-assembly placed more than once is then on that copy; default: the occurrence's first placement, or with no occurrence the placement nearest the pick), face: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a planar face) | circle: [x,y,z] | "<name>" (centre of a round end: a point on its wall or rim, the end's centre, or the round face's name as model.faces lists it) | edge: [x,y,z] (a point on an edge of a planar face: the edge's middle, z out of the face, y into it; on?: [x,y,z] a point on the face (default: the larger planar face beside the edge); corner?: [x,y,z] near one end: the corner there, x and y along its two edges into the face; found again by name, so it follows the face as it changes size; z?: [x,y,z] the frame's z instead of the face's normal, along the edge when it runs that way, x chosen from z: an edge or corner picked as it is, kept as a point where it can't be found by name) | point: [x,y,z], z?: [x,y,z] | plane: "XY"|"XZ"|"YZ"|"o:<ids>/origin/<item>"|"<name>" | axis: "X"|"Y"|"Z"|"o:<ids>/orig

material.assign.params: bodies: [names]; material: name (Steel, Aluminum, ABS Plastic, …, or one made with material.create; `material.list`)

material.create.params: name (not a built-in material's); density_g_cm3: (0, 1000]; appearance?: library name (appearance.library) | color?: "#rrggbb" or [r, g, b] (0–255), opacity? (0–1), pbr?: {metallic:0..1, roughness:0.045..1, dielectric_ior:1..3} (opaque only, needs color/appearance): the default look. A named appearance keeps its preset response when pbr is omitted; pbr: null selects scalar shading. Optical edits do not change density. physical_card?: validated SI candidate record (null/omitted means unknown); card density never changes assigned density. Assign it with material.assign

occurrence.copy.params: component (or occurrence): what to place again; path?: validates selected occurrence; parent?: component (default: the same parent); translate?: [x,y,z]; in_place?: bool (default false: the selected transform within the parent; true: where the selected placement is in the world, translate in world axes; a parent placed more than once is placed by parent_path?, else the active placement, and every instance gets the copy). Copies the selected effective transform, including pending moves

occurrence.ground.params: occurrence; grounded?: bool (default toggles) → grounded; transform: placement within its parent; moved: names of occurrences whose world placement changed; errors, conflicts: joint issues in the assembly solve

occurrence.move.params: occurrence; path?: exact placement; space?: local|world (default local); translate?: [x,y,z] (numbers or length expressions: an occurrence moved by expressions that name parameters keeps them and moves with them when the parameters change, along the axes the move was given in; other moves of it stay; a parameter they use can't be deleted, and a renamed one carries into them); axis?: [x,y,z], angle?: radians or "30 deg", origin?: [x,y,z] (numbers or length expressions, kept like translate's: the point the turn is about moves the part by what the turn leaves behind when a parameter in it changes); to?: {position: [x,y,z], axis?: [x,y,z], angle?} or to_matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (absolute placement: where it goes in space, not a move; not with translate/axis/angle/origin/matrix); matrix?: [12 or 16 numbers] (instead of translate/axis/angle/origin: a rigid move as a row-major 3x4 rotation-and-translation or 4x4 matrix, flat or as rows, its translation column (entries 4, 8 and 12) numbers or length expressions that are kept and followed like translate's; one that is a rotation only up to rounding is orthonormalised, a scale, shear or mirror is refused); tolerance?: largest accepted |Rᵀ

parameters.add.params: name, expression, unit?: as parameters.change (text: a text parameter, its expression the text), comment?, favorite?: bool

plastic.assign_rule.params: bodies: [names]; rule: name (empty: no rule) — plastic features on these bodies take its draft and clearance as defaults

plastic.manage_rules.params: name (library or new rule; a new one starts from `from`, default ABS (1.5mm)); from?; material?; thickness?, nominal_radius?, clearance?, knife_edge?, reveal_height?, thickness_variation?, draft?, max_thickness?, min_thickness?, min_draft? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's); active?: bool (rule for bodies without one); delete?: bool (a design rule; a library rule goes back to the library values)

sheet.manage_rules.params: name (new or existing); thickness?, k_factor?, bend_radius?, relief_width?, relief_depth?, corner_relief?, hem_gap?, gap? (expressions; `Thickness` is the rule's; gap: between flanges that meet at a corner, whose ends are closed toward each other at any angle); corner_relief_shape?: notch|round|rectangular|tear (what is cut where two bends meet at a corner of the base: round and rectangular a relief `corner_relief` across; tear none, each bend's end is cut straight from the corner to its flange's end; default notch); angle_display?: bend|included (how the DXF bend notes read the bend angles: the bend angle, default, or the included angle left between the bend's sides, 180° less it; the bend table gives both, and a flange's `angle` is always the bend angle); active?: bool; delete?: bool

timeline.add.params: feature: a feature as the design file and timeline.inspect hold it ({type, name?, id?, …}; the name is kept even when another feature has it, the id is kept and refused when another feature has it, so later steps can refer to them); params?: [{name, expression, unit?, comment?}] (the model parameters its sketch dimensions use); the feature goes at the marker → feature, name, error, warning
